relations.subject: server:node-recovery
relations.evidence: After failover has occurred, before the failed over node has been rebalanced out of the cluster, the node can be _recovered_, and thereby reintegrated into the cluster.

relations.subject: server:full-recovery
relations.evidence: There are two options for recovery, which are _full_ and _delta_.

relations.evidence: There are two options for recovery, which are _full_ and _delta_.

relations.subject: server:rebalance
relations.evidence: The row specifies `REBALANCE to finish full recovery`: therefore, left-click the **Rebalance** button to apply full recovery.

relations.subject: server:node-recovery
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call: recovery can be cancelled only up until the completing rebalance runs, captured here as recovery not supporting a cancellation path once rebalance has run
relations.evidence: Recovery can be aborted, by left-clicking on the **CANCEL ADD BACK** button.

relations.subject: server/8.0/manage/manage-nodes/recover-nodes
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - structural markdown link on the page
relations.evidence: There are two options for recovery, which are _full_ and _delta_. These are explained in [Recovery](../../learn/clusters-and-availability/recovery.md).

notable_absence.finding: This page names full and delta recovery as a closed pair and shows the API surface for choosing between them (recoveryType=full|delta) but never explains the actual mechanism difference itself - that is entirely deferred to learn/clusters-and-availability/recovery.md, which round 11-12's conceptual sweep may or may not have already covered (not verified in this batch, since that page is out of scope). This procedural page is therefore evidence that a real full/delta distinction exists and is REST/CLI-addressable, without itself being evidence of what the distinction consists of.
